title: Wedding of Mrs Fox: First Story
paragraphs: Once upon a time there was an old fox with nine tails who suspected that his wife wasn’t faithful to him, and he decided to test her. He stretched out under the bench, didn’t move a muscle, and acted as if he were stone dead. Mrs Fox went up to her room and locked herself in, while her maid, Miss Cat, sat by the fire and did the cooking. Once word got around that the old fox was dead, suitors started to appear. The maid heard someone at the front door, knocking. She went and opened it, and there stood a young fox, who said,

“What are you up to, Miss Cat?
Are you asleep, or are you awake?”

“I’m not asleep, I’m awake,
Want to know what I’m making?
I’m heating beer with butter in it,
Will you be my supper guest?”
“No, thank you, miss,” said the fox. “What is Mrs Fox doing?” The maid replied,

“She sits up in her room,
Crying in her gloom,
Weeping her little eyes red,
Because old Mr Fox is dead.”
“Please tell her, miss, that a young fox is here and would like to court her.” “Certainly, young sir.”

The cat goes up the stairs, trip, trap,
At the door she goes tap, tap, tap,
“Mistress Fox, are you in there?”
“Oh yes, my little cat,” she cried.
“A suitor is standing at the door.”
“And what does he look like, dear?”
“Does he have nine beautiful tails, like the late Mr Fox?” “Oh no,” answered the cat, “he has only one.” “Then I won’t have him.”

Miss Cat went downstairs and sent the suitor away. Soon there was another knock, and another fox stood at the door who wanted to court Mrs Fox. He had two tails, but he fared no better than the first. More came after that, each with one more tail than the one before, and all of them were turned away, until at last one came who had nine tails, just like old Mr Fox. When the widow heard this, she said happily to the cat,

“Now throw the gates and doors wide open,
And carry old Mr Fox right out.”
But just as the wedding was about to begin, old Mr Fox stirred under the bench, beat the whole rabble with a stick, and drove them and Mrs Fox out of the house.
